nodes_add.name: Hariharananda Tirthaswami (Nandakumar Vidyalankar)
nodes_add.note: Sanskrit scholar and Tantric teacher; taught Rammohan Sanskrit and, by biographers' accounts, initiated him into Tantric practice; stayed with him at Rangpur c. 1812

nodes_add.name: Ramchandra Vidyabagish
nodes_add.note: Sanskrit scholar and lexicographer; first secretary of the Brahmo Sabha (1828); kept services going after 1833; brought Debendranath Tagore into the Sabha's trust in 1843

nodes_add.name: Islamic theology and Persian learning
nodes_add.note: Rational and monotheist (tawhid) theology read in Arabic and Persian; shaped Rammohan's Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin (c. 1804). Merge with any Islam root if one exists

nodes_update.name: Rammohan Roy
nodes_update.note: Born 1772 (some sources 1774); Upanishad translations 1816–1819; founded the Brahmo Sabha, 20 August 1828; died Bristol 27 September 1833

edges_upsert.note: Vedanta Grantha (1815) and translations of Isha, Kena, Katha, Mundaka and Mandukya Upanishads (1816–1819)
Read the Brahma Sutras and Upanishads through Shankara's commentaries
Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin, Persian with Arabic preface; specific Mu'tazili link is B.N. Seal's interpretation
Precepts of Jesus (1820), Appeals (1820–1823); Unitarian reading; Calcutta Unitarian Committee with William Adam (1821)
Taught him Sanskrit in youth; biographers say he initiated him into Tantric practice
First secretary of the Brahmo Sabha; taught at Rammohan's Vedanta College
Brought Debendranath and about twenty Tattvabodhini members into the Brahmo Sabha trust, 7 Pous 1765 Shaka (December 1843)
Brahmo Sabha, revived by Debendranath as the Brahmo Samaj; Debendranath's father Dwarkanath was a trustee (1830)

places.name: Radhanagar
places.what: Birthplace (1772 or 1774), near Khanakul, Hooghly district

places.name: Murshidabad
places.what: Clerk to the Company; Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin published here c. 1804

places.name: Rangpur
places.what: Dewan to John Digby, c. 1809–1814; discussions on the unity of God

places.name: Kolkata (Chitpore Road, Brahmo Sabha)
places.what: Settled 1814; Atmiya Sabha 1815; Brahmo Sabha 1828, Chitpore Road building under the 1830 trust deed

places.name: Arnos Vale Cemetery, Bristol
places.what: Reburial 29 May 1843 under the chhatri funded by Dwarkanath Tagore; died at Stapleton nearby, 27 September 1833

glossary.def: The society of worshippers of Brahman, founded by Rammohan Roy in 1828 as the Brahmo Sabha; congregational worship of one formless God, without images.
A widow's self-immolation on her husband's funeral pyre, and the woman who does it; prohibited in Bengal on 4 December 1829.
Hymns to the formless Brahman sung in Brahmo worship; Rammohan wrote many of the first ones.
The oneness of God, the central doctrine of Islamic theology.

issues: rammohan-roy.mdx: birth year 1772 vs 1774 given as a range; death date 27 Sept 1833 in most sources, Haberman (Encyclopedia of Religion via encyclopedia.com) gives 22 Sept; used 27 Sept.
rammohan-roy.mdx: Atmiya Sabha 1815 (Banglapedia 'within a year' of mid-1814 arrival; Mitra 1815) vs 1814 (Wikipedia); text says '1815 (some sources say 1814)'.
rammohan-roy.mdx: sister-in-law sati story (1811) repeated by Mitra and others, not independently documented; hedged in text. Did not find a scholarly source explicitly doubting it.

rammohan-roy.mdx: Sumit Sarkar essay citation (V.C. Joshi ed., 1975) and Zastoupil book (Palgrave 2010, the 'If you read one book' pick) are cited from knowledge, not fetched; fact-checker should confirm bibliographic details.
rammohan-roy.mdx: sati tracts as two 'Conference' dialogues of 1818 and 1820 are from general knowledge plus Mitra's 'two dissertations'; dates should be confirmed.
rammohan-roy.mdx: Briggs attribution of the Bristol portrait is taken from the Art UK URL's artist filter; the page itself did not show the artist or date.
rammohan-roy.mdx: Dayananda's Calcutta visit given as 1872–1873 and his meeting with Keshab from general knowledge; coordinate with the dayananda-saraswati entry.
rammohan-roy.mdx: Radhanagar and Chitpore Road coordinates approximate (verified: false).
graph: added root 'islamic-theology'; merge with any Islam/Sufi root the author prefers. Existing 'sufi-orders' root not used since the Tuhfat's sources are rationalist theology, not a Sufi order.

rammohan-roy: Born 22 May 1772, Radhanagar, Hooghly; father Ramkanta (Vaishnava), mother Tarini Devi (Shaiva/Shakta family); sons Radhaprasad 1800, Ramaprasad 1812; second wife d. 1824 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Mohan_Roy
Patna Persian/Arabic at about nine, then Benares -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Mohan_Roy ; https://www.encyclopedia.com/international/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/roy-ram-mohan

Aristotle's logic and Euclid through Arabic; Calcutta by mid-1814; Sambad Kaumudi 1821; Mirat-ul-Akhbar 1822; title Raja from Akbar II; France 1832; d. Bristol 27 Sept 1833 -> https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Roy%2C_Raja_Rammohun

Nandakumar Vidyalankar = Hariharananda Tirthaswami, Tantric initiation, Rangpur c. 1812; Rangpur discussions; Digby from 1805 about nine years; Amherst letter 11 Dec 1823; Vedanta College 1826; 1811 sister-in-law sati story; arrival Liverpool April 1831 -> https://search.motherandsriaurobindo.in/_StaticContent/SriAurobindoAshram/-09 E-Library/-03 Disciples/Sisirkumar Mitra/-01 English/Resurgent India/-008_Forerunner.htm

Tuhfat c. 1804, Persian with Arabic preface, Murshidabad; 'zeburdast Maulavi'; quotes 'falsehood is common to all religions without distinction', 'an indispensable characteristic of man', 'custom and training make ... blind and deaf'; Hafiz; Seal's Mu'tazili view; Obaide translation 1883/1889 -> https://www.theindiaforum.in/article/rammohun-roys-gift
Vedanta Grantha 1815; Upanishad translations 1816-1819; Hindu Unitarian 1824-28 -> https://www.encyclopedia.com/international/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/roy-ram-mohan

Defence of Hindoo Theism 1817 answering Sankara Sastri in Madras Courier; quotes 'the doctrines of the unity of God are real Hindooism', 'numerous figures have been invented...', 'Many learned Brahmans are perfectly aware, of the absurdity of idol-worship', 'in his works of nature' -> https://franpritchett.com/00litlinks/txt_rammohunroy_hindu_theism.html

Precepts 1820; Marshman; Appeals 1820/1821/1823; William Adam, Calcutta Unitarian Committee 1821; Jesus 'superior even to the angels in heaven'; Lant Carpenter; Bentham, Godwin, Owen; meningitis -> https://www.uudb.org/roy-rammohun/

Brahmo Sabha first meeting 20 Aug 1828 at Feringhi Kamal Bose's house; Telugu Brahmins recite Vedas, Utsavananda explains in Bengali, Brahmasangeet; 1843 covenant via Vidyabagish -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahmo_Samaj

Trust deed 8 Jan 1830, Chitpore Road; quotes 'Eternal Unsearchable and Immutable Being...', 'no graven image statue or sculpture...', 'all sorts and descriptions of people without distinction', 'reviled or slightingly or contemptuously spoken of' -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trust_Deed_of_Brahmo_Sabha
Ramchandra Vidyabagish 1786-1845, first secretary 1828, initiated Debendranath 1843 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Chandra_Vidyabagish
Sati Regulation 4 Dec 1829; Dharma Sabha, Radhakanta Deb; Privy Council upheld -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Sati_Regulation,_1829

Gandhi April 1921 Orissa 'contagion of English learning', 'pygmies'; Tagore to Andrews 10 May 1921 'I strongly protest...' -> https://franpritchett.com/00litlinks/txt_guha_bilingual_intellectual_2010.html
Autobiographical letter quotes; Collet calls it 'spurious' (Sandford Arnot, Athenaeum 5 Oct 1833) -> https://d11.thedailystar.net/opinion/focus/news/raja-rammohun-roy-autobiographical-sketch-3028591

Burial Stapleton Grove 18 Oct 1833; reburial Arnos Vale 29 May 1843; chhatri with Dwarkanath Tagore; Derrett on Mahanirvana Tantra 'highly improbable' -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Mohan_Roy ; https://arnosvale.org.uk/the-raja-reformer-radical-and-religious/
Hatcher, Hinduism Before Reform (2020), reviewed by Tanika Sarkar -> https://www.theindiaforum.in/article/prehistory-religious-modernity
Portrait oil on canvas, Bristol Museum & Art Gallery -> https://artuk.org/discover/artworks/rajah-rammohun-roy-17721833-188130/search/actor:briggs-henry-perronet-179117931844/page/1/view_as/list
Collet, Life and Letters, Calcutta 1914 ed. -> https://archive.org/details/lifelettersofraj00collrich/page/n5/mode/2up
